title: The engine holds only one egress timestamp: a second stamp before dispatch destroys the first
body:
[A1] Found while establishing the premise for a fix to #28, and measured at `main` `03ad3caf`. Independent of #28: #28 is about which pending transmission a stamp is credited to, this is about the engine being able to hold only one stamp at all. They interact, because two outstanding frames is the case that produces two stamps, but neither causes the other.

## What is wrong

The engine keeps exactly one egress timestamp, and it samples its value when the event is dispatched rather than when the stamp arrives. A second stamp arriving before the first is dispatched destroys the first.

- `hdl/top/KL_gptp_engine.sv:179`, `logic [63:0] txts_r;` is a single register, written unconditionally on every stamp at `:196` (`if (txts_valid_i) txts_r <= txts_ns_i;`).
- `:231-232` hold a single pending flag and a single sequence, `txts_pend_r` and `txts_pend_seq_r`, set together at `:278-280`; a second stamp overwrites the sequence while the flag is already set, so only one EV_TX_TS event is ever pushed for the pair.
- `:349` samples the value AT DISPATCH, `disp_ts0_r <= (ev_head_w[39:32] == EV_TX_TS_C) ? txts_r : ...`, so the event carries whatever `txts_r` holds when it dispatches, not what it held when the stamp was captured.
- `:327-328` gates dispatch on `ser_idle_w` and the uCPU being ready, so dispatch is blocked exactly while another frame is being built or serialized.

## Measured

At `03ad3caf`, in a throwaway worktree, RTL and ucode unmodified. A peer Pdelay_Req is answered so a Pdelay_Resp is outstanding, then two stamps are fed with a swept gap and the resulting Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up's `t3` says which one survived:

```text
gap  0 cycles   Resp_FU carries the SECOND stamp: the first is lost
gap  1 cycle    first stamp kept
gap  2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 20, 50 cycles   first stamp kept
```

So the margin is the dispatch latency. It is one cycle while the engine is idle. It is not one cycle while the engine is mid-build or mid-serialize, because `:327` blocks the pop then, and I have not bounded it in that state from this repository.

## Impact

Whenever two of the plane's frames are outstanding at once, which is the ordinary case this engine already creates (our cadence Pdelay_Req and a Pdelay_Resp to a peer, since dispatch is gated only on `ser_idle_w` and a new build may start while an earlier frame's stamp has not returned), the two stamps race the dispatch. If they arrive closer together than the dispatch latency, one exchange silently gets the other's timestamp: a Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up carries a `t3` that is not its own, or our `t1` is replaced. Nothing counts it and nothing detects it.

The separation between two stamps is a property of the parent's fabric, not of this repository: the second frame's transmission across the 64-bit lane at the MAC boundary is what spaces them, and the merge arbiter and gasket set how much more. That is measurable only on the parent side.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Two stamps arriving with any separation, including adjacent cycles, are both delivered to the ucode with their own values, either by buffering stamps in the engine, for example a short FIFO of {ts, seq} beside the event queue, or by a stated and tested minimum separation the fabric guarantees, with the engine refusing or counting anything closer rather than silently taking the newer value.
- [ ] Engine test: with two frames outstanding, two stamps fed at a 0-cycle gap leave each exchange with its own timestamp, and the sweep above stays green at every gap; a planted mutation restoring the single register or the dispatch-time sample goes red; README counts updated.
- [ ] If the chosen answer is a guaranteed separation rather than a buffer, the guarantee is written down here and the parent measures it on hardware, since the donor bench drives `txts_valid_i` itself and cannot establish it.
- [ ] Whatever it costs is reported against the ROM and LUT budgets, which are 929 of 1,024 words and 3,116 LUT at `03ad3caf`.

Related: #28 (the shared pending cell, the case that creates two outstanding frames), #26 (PR #29), kebag-logic/milan-fpga#213.
